ios.body: App Total Install is -2.0% while the other steps are all moving about +11.7% — a gap of -13.7pp. When one step moves very differently from the rest, the cause is usually specific to that step.

ios.head: Expect App Total Revenue to recover in about 7 days — more of the people installing are subscribing.
ios.body: App Total New Subs is +11.7% while App Total Install is only -2.0% — a bigger share of people who installed are subscribing than usual (+13.7pp more growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to go up in about 7 days. App Total Revenue is -8.0% right now, so this points to a recovery rather than more weakness.

insights.title: Install source — App Total Install -16.2% — Organic Install is behind most of it (-2,749, -22.9%).
insights.body: App Total Install was 20,788, against 24,821 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of -4,033. Where that came from: Organic Install -2,749 (-22.9%), Paid Install -1,008 (-9.4%), SEO Install -227 (-14.0%). Organic Install moved the most on its own (-2,749, -22.9%) and is now 44.5% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue -12.1% — down in line with the new subs signed up 7 days earlier (-7.2%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 11-10 vs 11-03 is -12.1%, and App Total New Subs on 11-03 vs 10-27 was -7.2% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (on 11-10 vs 11-03): Subscription -11.8%, Pay as you go -16.4%. The drop was already visible in new subs a week ago, so lifting new subs now is what turns revenue around next week.

insights.title: Revenue by purchase type — App Total Revenue -7.4% — down mainly in Subscription (-5,115, -7.4%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue was 68,339, against 73,838 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks (-5,499). By purchase type: Subscription -5,115 (-7.4%), Pay as you go -384 (-9.0%). Pay as you go is 5.7% of revenue. Subscription is the recurring part fed by new subs about a week earlier; look at new subs and renewals.

insights.title: Purchase type by app — Subscription revenue is falling most in YCP (-10.4%).
insights.body: By app: the biggest Subscription fall is YCP -2,895 (-10.4%, about 37% of revenue); Pay as you go moved most in YCP -645 (-46.6%); YCV relies most on Pay as you go (14% of its revenue vs 5.7% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Which app — App Total Install -16.2% is mostly YCP — not every app.
insights.body: App Total Install moved -16.2% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -16.2%, YMK +4.5%, YCP -93.2%, YCV -2.9%). YCP accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Purchase type by country — Subscription revenue is falling most in JP (-23.9%), while TR grows (+25.4%).
insights.body: By country: the biggest Subscription fall is JP -824 (-23.9%, about 6% of revenue); the biggest Subscription gain is TR +432 (+25.4%); Pay as you go moved most in US +267 (+21.1%); JP relies most on Pay as you go (32% of its revenue vs 5.7% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Market trend — GB is losing ground fast on turning installs into subs (-46.6%, now 14.0%).
insights.body: In GB, 14.0% of installs now turn into new subs — -46.6% versus last period. It is about 5% of revenue (a market worth watching): fewer of the people downloading are subscribing, and revenue will feel that within a week or two.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — YCP is turning installs into New Subs better than usual (-54.0% vs Install -93.2%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YCP New Subs -54.0% vs Install -93.2% (better than its installs); YCV New Subs +2.7% vs Install -2.9% (better than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

insights.title: Which country — US is out of line with every other country on App Total Revenue (+1.3% vs -7.4%).
insights.body: For All App, App Total Revenue in US is +1.3% while all countries together are -7.4% — a gap of +8.8pp. US is about 43% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.
